sentences: A woman with a long face fills the canvas and looks straight back at us.
Orange shadows on her cheekbones make her look strong, yet her large, deep eyes seem unsettled and her tightly closed mouth is in shade.
The dark green jacket, silver-grey collar and wavy hair are the look of a 1920s 'New Woman'.
Na Hye-seok is often called Korea's first woman painter in Western oils, and in 1921 she held a solo show of oil paintings in Seoul.
The portrait is thought to date from her stay in Paris during a 1927 trip to Europe, and its dark, flat brushwork breaks with the brighter Impressionist manner of her earlier work.
Her family always knew it as a self-portrait, though some scholars think the face differs from her photographs, and her descendants gave it to the Suwon Museum of Art in 2015.
